title: Tax Salience: How Requiring Transparency Affects the Price of Equality
abstract: arXiv:2605.30081v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Less-salient taxes can ease the classic trade-off between equality and efficiency by making people respond less to taxation. But deliberately obscuring taxes may be viewed as dishonest. This creates a three-way trade-off between equality, efficiency, and honesty. We analyze this trade-off in a simple setting with a linear income tax. We define and characterize the morally efficient frontier, trading off utilitarian welfare against honesty or transparency. Complete honesty is Pareto inefficient but not morally inefficient. More generally, increasing honesty reduces utilitarian welfare. When utilitarian welfare is decomposed into equality and efficiency, the cost of honesty falls most robustly on equality: Higher salience always reduces equality, while the effect on efficiency is ambiguous. translated_title: 税收显著性：要求透明度如何影响平等的代价
translated_abstract: 较低显著性的税收可以通过使人们对税收的反应降低，来缓解平等与效率之间的经典权衡。但故意模糊税收可能被视为不诚实。这在平等、效率与诚实之间形成了三方权衡。我们在一个采用线性所得税的简单设定中分析这一权衡。我们定义并刻画了“道德效率前沿”，在功利主义福利与诚实（或透明度）之间进行权衡。完全诚实是帕累托低效的，但并非道德上低效。更一般而言，提高诚实度会降低功利主义福利。当将功利主义福利分解为平等和效率时，诚实的成本最稳健地落在平等上：更高的显著性总是降低平等，而对效率的影响则不明确。这种不对称性源于显著性提高了“平等的代价”，即平等边际增加所带来的效率成本。
tldr: 该论文定义并刻画了税收领域中的“道德效率前沿”，分析透明度在平等、效率与诚实之间的三方权衡，并发现税收显著性的成本最稳健地落在平等上——更高的显著性总是降低平等，而对效率的影响则不明确。
en_tdlr: This paper defines and characterizes the "morally efficient frontier" in taxation, analyzing the three-way trade-off between equality, efficiency, and honesty, and shows that the cost of tax salience falls most robustly on equality: higher salience always reduces equality while its effect on efficiency is ambiguous.
